Dear \_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_,

My name is \_\_\_\_\_ and I am a contributor for [geolab](http://geolab.wm.edu), a data science research lab at the College of William & Mary in the United States. We recently announced the release of [geoBoundaries](https://www.geoboundaries.org/), an open source geospatial data extraction tool provided to the research and analyst community. This tool has freely been used by thousands of policy analysts, program evaluators, and scientists to conduct analyses of development policies and programs using geospatial data.  It allows anyone to easily obtain datasets that fuse together georeferenced data on development investments with a battery of other measures from satellites, surveys, and weather stations.

A critical limitation of this tool is that we are currently using geographic administrative boundaries with many known errors. As such, we are reaching out to our in-country partners, GIS practitioners, and others in the field to construct a fully open-source boundary dataset to both (a) integrate into the GeoQuery tool, and (b) release as a public good.  As we went through this process, we came across the shapefile you uploaded to the \_\_\_\_\_Source\_\_\_\_\_\_ for \_\_\_\_\_Country\_\_\_\_\_\_. This email is to seek your permission to redistribute these shapefiles under an open source license which will enable other researchers to download and use your boundary information with minimal restrictions. If you are open to our use and distribution of your boundary information, we would deeply appreciate a response to this email providing an affirmation.

Finally, if you have any additional information on individuals we might contact for more up-to-date information (if it exists), we would welcome such information.
